Industry observers note that apple only rolled out high-end ‘Pro’ and ‘Duo’ iPhones this fall, marking a departure from previous years when more affordable models debuted too. But iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 are still coming, and a latest report offers an update on release timing.

A newly introduced report from Kim Yeong-ho at ETNews provides a fresh update on timing for the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2.

Rumors have indicated for well over a year that Apple planned to push these models out of the typical fall launch window and introduce them in early 2027 instead.

Sources indicate that per ETNews, Samsung and LG are providing the display panels for the new models, with Samsung the sole supplier for iPhone Air 2 and both companies splitting orders for iPhone 18. And their mass production intends signal a March release for the products.

Kim Yeong-ho, writing at ETNews:.

Samsung Display plans to begin mass production in January, while LG Display will start late this year…The Korean panel makers appear to be aligning their production plans with an expected March launch.

A March launch window lines up well with when Apple tends to ramp up product introductions following a slower winter. Earlier this year, iPhone 17e debuted in March alongside upcoming Macs and the iPad Air.

The year before, however, the iPhone 16e arrived in February instead.

In a recent development, with Apple shaking up its normal iPhone rollout schedule, it was anyone’s guess how soon the upcoming models would debut. But a March launch makes sense and gives Apple a trio of new iPhones every six months—three unveiled in September, and another three in March.

#50950. How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (2956 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2956 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • It has been revealed that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

It has been revealed that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

In a recent development, the tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully released on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

According to recent reports, this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

“I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” claims Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Industry observers note that phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Recent findings suggest that scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

More than 10 years in the making, MMX introduced on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

In a recent development, if all goes according to proposal, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” indicates Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Sources indicate that once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to blueprint, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” claims Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

According to recent reports, during its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

In a recent development, before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu claims, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

“It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

In a recent development, A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Industry observers note that once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she indicates. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday notes.

Industry observers note that despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday indicates Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Industry observers note that idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec claims. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

According to recent reports, what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

Sources indicate that the MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

According to recent reports, the coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel states. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this problem and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu notes.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

Industry observers note that during the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Sources indicate that finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel indicates. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

“MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu notes. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Apple Store in Hamburg, Germany.

According to recent reports, jon McCormack, Apple’s head of camera and photo software, retired at the end of October after more than eight years, Bloomberg reported. Apple has not named a replacement, and his deputies are taking over his work under other executives.

Recent findings suggest that jon McCormack, the Apple executive in charge of the iPhone’s Camera and Photos software, has retired, Bloomberg reported on Thursday. He left at the end of October after more than eight years at the manufacturer, according to people familiar with the matter.

Apple has not named a new vice president for his role. His former deputies are taking on his work under other executives, Bloomberg said. An Apple spokesperson declined to comment.

In a recent development, mcCormack oversaw the software behind how iPhone customers take, view and edit photos and videos. His team worked on the redesigned selfie camera in the iPhone 17 and the upcoming camera controls this year, when the iPhone 18 Pro got Apple’s first variable-aperture camera.

According to recent reports, he was a strong opponent of using generative AI to create or alter photos, people inside Apple told Bloomberg. Google and Samsung have leaned into AI tools that can make big changes to images.

“A photograph is of something that actually happened,” McCormack told Wired earlier this year.

Recent findings suggest that unlike its rivals, Apple added a mode that lets the iPhone 18 Pro prove photos are real. Bloomberg’s sources mentioned his retirement was not linked to any clash over Apple’s AI strategy.

It has been revealed that mcCormack reported to software chief Craig Federighi, whose team is under pressure to speed up AI work. He follows Apple Pay head Jennifer Bailey out the door this autumn, as fresh CEO John Ternus cuts management layers to move faster.

iOS 27.3 rolls out next month and includes several exciting changes for iPhone Duo, here’s what’s new for Apple’s foldable model.

Apple is granting iPhone Duo people one of their biggest feature requests: face unlock is coming with iOS 27.3.

In a recent development, face unlock isn’t a full-fledged Face ID, and it doesn’t work for features like Apple Pay, but it is a convenient upcoming option for unlocking your iPhone Duo just by looking at it. Per Apple:.

Use the front camera, along with a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, to rapidly unlock iPhone Duo when it’s closed. Face recognition data never leaves your device.

If your iPhone Duo has gone unused for 45 minutes or more, face unlock won’t work and you’ll need to authenticate with Touch ID or your passcode. But for most people, that probably just means using Touch ID first thing in the morning, then relying on face unlock the rest of the day.

On a related note, you can also enable Attention Aware features in iOS 27.3. These are available whether you use the face unlock feature or not, but are limited to the outer display. Once enabled, they can automatically lower the volume of alarms and timers, keep the display from dimming, and more.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds upcoming face unlock feature for iPhone Duo.

In a recent development, reachability is available on other iPhone models to move onscreen content down vertically, closer to your thumb. But on iPhone Duo with iOS 27.3, Apple has a unique twist on the feature.

Instead of helping you reach content vertically, Reachability on iPhone Duo works horizontally.

If you’re using the outer screen and find that buttons or other UI elements are out of reach, you can swipe from the side to have onscreen content shift closer to your thumb.

In a recent development, you can always disable Reachability if you find yourself accidentally triggering it too often. But if one-handed iPhone Duo use gives you trouble, Reachability is a great new option to have.

Read more: iOS 27.3 introduces fresh iPhone Duo feature for one-handed use.

In a recent development, what should happen when you close your iPhone Duo’s folding screen? Apple has found that users have different preferences. Some want the iPhone to stay unlocked for continued use, while others prefer that it automatically locks when closed.

In iOS 27.3, Apple adds a upcoming setting so users can enable whichever behavior they prefer.

By default, iPhone Duo will work as it always has, staying unlocked after being closed. But inside Settings ⇾ Display & Brightness, iOS 27.3 provides the option of automatically locking upon being closed instead. You could achieve something similar before with Shortcuts, but now there’s a built-in setting too.

It’s not exactly a “fresh feature,” but iPhone Duo owners will also find that the system keyboard has changed in iOS 27.3. Apple tweaked the outer display keyboard to push keys closer together and make one-handed use easier.

Here’s a comparison of the old and upcoming keyboards via Beta Profiles on X:.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 beta tweaks iPhone Duo's outer display keyboard, with narrower keys and a slightly thinner, smaller font. pic.twitter.com/BDKCBZc52Z.

Read more: iOS 27.3 changes the iPhone Duo keyboard, here’s how.

Type: Down alternativeBest for: Side sleepers, hot sleepersSizes: Standard Loft: 4-5 inches height, High Loft: 6-7 inches heightTrial: 45 nightsWarranty: 1-yearPrice: $95 at Saatva.

I never once got hot or sweaty sleeping on this pillow thanks to a cotton cover and a down alternative fill that allowed air to circulate through at night.

The standard loft is a bouncy, plump pillow, and while it's not firm in the traditional sense, there isn't much give to the surface. I imagine this pillow will retain its shape for a good amount of time.

I slept most comfortably on my side with this pillow, even though it was just a tad too tall for me. Stomach sleeping isn’t possible with the Down Alternative Pillow, but if you like your head being slightly lifted when sleeping on your back, this pillow is for you.

Industry observers note that it’s not the most comfortable pillow I’ve tested, but I think that has more to do with my body size not fitting with the pillow. I’m particularly glad it was hypoallergenic, as I tested it in the fall when my seasonal allergies were already triggered. Starting at $95, this pillow is on the high end for a down alternative pillow whose height isn’t adjustable, but at least it comes with a 45-day free trial.

The Saatva Down Alternative Pillow starts at $95 for a queen size in standard loft. Down alternative pillows are usually more affordable than this, ranging from $20-$75. If I had to guess, the price comes from the brand name more than anything else. We see the same pricing for similar down alternative pillows sold by Boll & Branch and SlumberCloud. I’d probably wait for a Saatva sale to grab this pillow; in its current Black Friday sale you can save $40 when you buy a pair of standard pillows.

Recent findings suggest that at least Saatva offers a 45-night trial with free returns and a 1-year limited warranty for this pillow. The 45-night trial is longer than most pillow warranties, so that’s a good perk for the price.

The Saatva Down Alternative Pillow is a breathable pillow with a cotton cover, hypoallergenic fill, and a bouncy, plump surface. Buyers receive a 1-year warranty and 45-night trial. The $95 price tag is somewhat high for a pillow made with alternative down, but during major sales you can often save when you buy a pair of pillows.

The Saatva Down Alternative Pillow is simply made. You can order it in two different lofts — standard or high — and in a queen or king size. The standard loft has a 4 or 5 inch height, while the high loft is 6 to 7 inches tall.

Industry observers note that I received the standard loft size and when measured, it came out to a little over 7 inches tall. I can only imagine how tall the high loft option is.

According to Saatva, with the standard loft, you should be able to sleep in any position (including your stomach), while the high loft is better for side and combination sleepers.

The 100% sateen cotton cover has 400 thread count, and the interior is comprised of Versaloft recycled down alternative fibers. The recycled fibers make this pillow hypoallergenic.

Keep reading to learn more about how the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow performed over the course of a week of testing.

Industry observers note that the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow arrived in a large cardboard box. Inside, I found the pillow zipped inside a white bag with handles. When I removed it from the bag, I didn’t notice any smells. The pillow was ready to sleep on immediately.

It has been revealed that one look at the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow and I was pretty sure that I’d only be able to sleep on my side on it. Soon I discovered that I was right.

According to recent reports, I tested the standard loft size, and as mentioned, it was a little over two inches taller than Saatva advertised. No wonder I found the pillow plumper and taller than the pillows I normally use. Upon lying on the pillow, my head barely sunk into the thick, bouncy surface. It did not contour around my head.

It has been revealed that I placed a 15lb. dumbbell on the pillow, and it sank in about an inch. (The average weight of a head is 10-12 lbs.) Upon removal, the pillow bounced swiftly back to its full size.

When lying on my side, my head didn’t sink into the pillow that much. However, when lying on my back, my head slowly sunk down a bit further, but not enough to really align my neck and spine. It was the kind of position that I like to be in when I’m congested or sick — with my neck and head tilted upward. Normally, however, I would not find that position comfortable.

I attempted to sleep on my stomach on this pillow, but I just slipped off. Since I can sleep on my side, I took up that position most nights, but unfortunately, I found that the loft (even the Standard Loft) was slightly too high to achieve a comfortable sleep. Perhaps my shoulders are too narrow.

According to recent reports, that’s not to say that there is something wrong with this pillow, only that the width of my shoulders might not be long enough to fit this pillow when lying on my side. As the pillow softens over time, it could adjust into something that fits my body better. I think someone who is larger than me or at least broader in their shoulders, would like this pillow.

I’ve slept on down and alternative down pillows before, and I have to say that I prefer the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow because I suffer from allergies. The hypoallergenic nature of the pillow really aided me during testing since I was dealing with seasonal allergies and hay fever.

During testing, I didn’t get hot or sweaty sleeping on this pillow — which makes sense considering the materials. It’s filled with Versaloft down alternative fill: recycled fibers that allow air to flow through. The 100% cotton cover also played a role in keeping me cool and moisture-free overnight as it’s one of the most breathable materials on the market. While testing, I used a linen pillow cover which ensured I never once woke up hot.

Recent findings suggest that no matter the pillow, you’ll probably need to replace it after two years. If your pillow resists being folded in half and bounces back quickly, there's still plenty of life left in it, otherwise, search for a latest one as the fill has worn down.

I slept on at Standard Loft Saatva Down Alternative Pillow for a week and did not see any indication of the pillow sagging or lowering its loft. In fact, I kept hoping that the pillow’s loft would ease up a bit so I could sleep on it more comfortably, but that was never the case.

Sources indicate that the pillow feels sturdy and durable, and I expect it to last you a full two years. The one-year limited warranty is fairly average across the industry.

Some people don’t realize that they need to care for their pillow to keep it in good shape and get their money’s worth. I’m glad to report that caring for the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow is easier than most.

For one, you don’t have to plump this pillow each day. It retained its shape as soon as I removed my head.

To get rid of stains or just to clean your pillow of the oils and fluids from your hair, face, or mouth, you can machine wash it on cold, as long as you do so separately from your other clothes. Once the pillow is done washing, Saatva suggests running an extra spin cycle to remove as much water as possible, since you’ll have to tumble dry the pillow on low until it’s fully dry (which could take quite a while).

The Saatva Down Alternative Pillow is a good choice for those with broader shoulders or who like a plump pillow that doesn't allow their head to sink in. That's not the kind of pillow experience I prefer, but I can't deny that there aren't some great qualities to this pillow.

It comes in two different loft sizes, so sleepers can choose the one that best fits their size and preference. Unfortunately I found the standard size to be taller (by 2-3 inches) than advertised, so keep that in mind when ordering.

The bouncy, supportive feel isn't firm, but the pillow won't let your head sink in when lying on your side or stomach, which are the most ideal sleep positions for this pillow (no matter what Saatva advertises).

A temperature-neutral sleep is the best thing the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow offers. You won't wake up sweaty or hot because the recycled fibers and cotton cover are so breathable and wick moisture away at night. Not to mention, the recycled fibers won't trigger any sleep allergies. If all that wasn't enough, you can also throw the pillow into your washing machine, making the care and maintenance for this pillow easier than others.

Truthfully, a $95 starting price is on the high end for a down alternative pillow, but at least the pillow comes with a 45-night trial with free returns which gives buyers some peace of mind.

✅ You're a hot sleeper: The cotton cover and down alternative fill makes this a very breathable pillow resulting in a neutral night’s sleep.

✅ You're a side or back sleeper: The higher loft (even with the standard loft size) and supportive feel makes it a good choice for side and back sleepers, especially since you won’t sink too much into this pillow.

✅ You have allergies: If you like the feel of a down pillow but hate waking with a stuffy nose, this down alternative pillow won’t trigger your allergies.

❌ You sleep on your stomach: While back and side sleepers could find comfort with this pillow, it’s too tall and doesn’t have enough give for stomach sleepers — which is why I slipped off every time I tried to sleep on my stomach.

❌ You have narrow shoulders: Most side sleepers will be supported by the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow, but since the pillow doesn’t have much give, it could be too tall for those with narrow shoulders.

❌ You want the ability to adjust your pillow height: The pillow may soften over time, but it’ll take months for that happen. If you prefer to adjust the height of your pillow from day one, like with the Coop Sleep Goods pillow, then the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow is not for you.

A $60 price tag feels a lot more realistic for a down alternative pillow, which is why you might consider the Beckham Hotel Collection Original Down Alternative Pillow. It’s a good choice for side and back sleepers and will keep you temperature neutral at night. Our reviewers aren’t as confident about its long-term durability, and they were disappointed by a lack of a sleep trial and warranty.

Sources indicate that the Saatva Latex Pillow is one of our editor’s top picks for its breathability, comfort, and benefits for sleepers with allergies. The fill is made with shredded latex, which allows air to flow through at night. The cover is washable and you can order the pillow in two loft heights. It provides a huggable sleep feel so your head sinks in more compared to the Down Alternative Pillow. At $165, the Saatva Latex Pillow is more expensive, but may be worth the investment.

It has been revealed that those who don’t have allergies could consider the Helix Down & Feather Pillow. This plush and fluffy pillow is often discounted to $79, making it more affordable than the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow. It is better suited to side sleepers or back sleepers who like a higher loft, though interestingly enough, it has more of a sink-in feel resulting in a softer sleep experience. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that hyperLogLog (HLL) is the standard textbook choice.
  • While evaluating alternatives, I came across Apache DataSketches, which offered a battle-tested HllSketch alongside CpcSketch, an even more space-efficient design.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It started with a routine feature in ScopeDB: implementing approx_count_distinct for approximate distinct counting.

Sources indicate that hyperLogLog (HLL) is the standard textbook choice. Early on, Rustâs HLL ecosystem was uneven, so I started with Cloudflareâs open-source cardinality-estimator. That crate leaned heavily on unsafe code and manual bit-packing tricks, though, so to keep things auditable and under our control, I forked and maintained an internal copy inside ScopeDB.

While evaluating alternatives, I came across Apache DataSketches, which offered a battle-tested HllSketch alongside CpcSketch, an even more space-efficient design. At the time, Apache DataSketches only shipped Java and C++ implementations, whereas ScopeDB is written in Rust.

Industry observers note that as it turned out, the Apache DataSketches community was interested in an official Rust port. Starting late last year, I teamed up with a few other Rust developers well-versed in sketching algorithms to build and ship the initial releases of datasketches-rust, beginning with HllSketch. Soon after, I switched ScopeDBâs distinct counting over to our datasketches-rust implementation.

In a recent development, anyone who has implemented streaming distinct counting knows how HLL works: elements are hashed into KKK buckets, and each bucket keeps only the maximum leading-zero count seen so far (typically 4 to 6 bits), while every other hit in that bucket goes unrecorded. Once HLL enters dense mode, every bucket maintains a fixed-width register.

In a recent development, in his 2017 paper Back to the Future: an Even More Nearly Optimal Cardinality Estimation Algorithm, Yahoo! Research scientist Kevin J. Lang proposed going back to basics: instead of keeping only per-bucket maxima, retain the full KÃ64K \times 64KÃ64 bit matrix of the classic FM85 coupon collectorâs process. Whenever row rrr sees a hash with ccc leading zeros, set bit (r,c)(r, c)(r,c) to 111. Keeping the full two-dimensional hit matrix lets CPC pair a streaming HIP estimator with a mergeable ICON estimator for higher statistical efficiency than HLL. On serialization, it adapts its layout to fill density: low cardinalities use a sparse PairTable of (row, column) pairs, while medium and high cardinalities combine a sliding 8-bit window, length-limited Huffman coding, and column permutations to pack the sketch near the information-theoretic entropy limit. According to the DataSketches documentation, serialized CPC shrinks storage by 30% to 40% compared with HLL at equal accuracy.

In late January, I ported CpcSketch to datasketches-rust (PR-75) and switched ScopeDB over to it. It has run smoothly in production for more than six months.

While porting CpcSketch from the upstream C++ and Java implementations, however, I noticed several hardcoded magic lookup tables in the source code:.

It has been revealed that these four sets of static tables live in compression_data.rs and estimator.rs. Here is a short excerpt:.

Whenever I port lookup tables, I prefer to derive the values from first principles in unit tests and check them element by element against the static array. For kxp_byte_lookup, for example, I kept the derivation right inside the test suite:.

In a recent development, for CompressionData and the ICON estimator tables, though, no generator source existed anywhere in the repositories, so I had no way to derive them on my own back then. Only two build commands remained in an upstream comment:.

In a recent development, I searched every Apache DataSketches repository and came up empty on those .ml files. So I opened CONCERN-720 on datasketches-java to ask where the generator sources lived. Lee Rhodes replied:.

Kevin did most of his math simulations and modeling in OCaml. And his code was on his computer, which no longer exists. And his personal code died with him â¦ even if they have a copy of his old computer it might be trying to find a needle in a haystack.

Kevin passed away in April 2019, and any code left on his personal machine is effectively lost to history.

Sources indicate that I was saddened to hear that. Kevinâs research in sketching algorithms underpins many of the core sketches in Apache DataSketches:.

Recent findings suggest that still, with the runtime decoders and detailed header comments sitting right there in the source files, it seemed possible to reverse-engineer the offline generators from the artifacts alone. I asked Lee whether the CPC paper explained how the tables were derived, and he answered:.

In a recent development, you should definitely read the paper. But it wonât tell you any details on the Huffman codings. As I recall, in his paper he used a more standard compression scheme. He finished his work on the code after he had finished his paper â and in the process came up with the modified Huffman coding idea, which is quite a bit more efficient than what he discussed in the paper.

That placed the derivation well beyond what I could work out on my own in an afternoon.

Since CpcSketch worked fine in datasketches-rust as long as the lookup arrays were copied faithfully, I left the mystery aside for the time being.

According to recent reports, then Gemini 4 Carbon came out just as I was preparing the next release of datasketches-rust. Since the checked-in tables and 20-digit header comments already acted as a strict numerical oracle, any candidate generator could be tested immediately in code: either it reproduced every codeword, permutation entry, and floating-point diagnostic within IEEE-754 precision, or it was wrong. That made the problem well suited to an agentic workflow built around executable checks and adversarial review.

Over several iterations, I steered three models against that oracle and against one another:.

None of the models got everything right on the first try, and several plausible-looking explanations collapsed as soon as we tested perturbations in code. What survived that filter became PR-355, which checks the reconstructed generators and derivations into datasketches-rust as unit tests, following the same approach we took for kxp_byte_lookup.

The rest of this post focuses on the mathematics and numerical forensics behind those four sets of tables: how each structure works, which wrong turns looked convincing until an ablation broke them, and where the surviving artifacts cannot tell two models apart. Formal derivations sit in the appendix at the end; if you spot an error, feel free to leave a comment or open a PR on datasketches-rust.

We begin with the 23 Huffman coding tables in compression_data.rs.

Recent findings suggest that why hardcode 23 static Huffman tables at all? Building trees dynamically per sketch would force the serializer to write tree headers into the compressed stream, wiping out the tens of bytes saved on small sketches. Meanwhile, the probability that column jjj of the coupon matrix is set depends mainly on the fill ratio C/KC / KC/K (collected coupons CCC over row count KKK). Finite-KKK corrections enter only at order 1/K1 / K1/K, a tiny difference that turns out to be the key clue below. Precomputing optimal tables offline across representative C/KC / KC/K checkpoints lets determine_pseudo_phase select the right table solely from lg_k and num_coupons without storing a table ID.

Industry observers note that the first 22 tables encode 8-bit sliding-window bytes (000 through 255255255). Given the per-column bit probabilities q0q_0q0â through q7q_7q7â for the 8 adjacent columns in the window (treated as independent), byte bbb has theoretical probability equal to the product of eight Bernoulli terms: qdq_dqdâ if bit ddd is 111, and 1âqd1 - q_d1âqdâ if bit ddd is 000.

According to recent reports, in the steady-state regime, columns left of the sliding window are nearly all 111, while columns to the right are nearly all 000. The remaining 56 out-of-window columns therefore store only surprising bits, namely zeros left of the window or ones right of the window, encoded via column index deltas. Putting higher-probability surprising columns first keeps unary deltas short, which is what the 16 56-byte tables from generatePermutationsForSLIDING.ml accomplish.

That layout alone pins down BBB: in the first six tables (phase indices 0..5), three trailing slots correspond to columns left of the window and get interleaved upward; in the last ten tables, that count jumps to four. Two practical hurdles arise immediately: how to run 10610^6106 trials across lg_k = 4..=14 on a single machine, and why todayâs numbers match Kevinâs original integers as closely as they do.

Simulating individual insertions naively at lg_k =14= 14=14 (K=16384K = 16384K=16384) takes 1.6Ã1071.6 \times 10^71.6Ã107 steps per trial (1.6Ã10131.6 \times 10^{13}1.6Ã1013 iterations across 10610^6106 trials), which is impractical on a single machine. Our fast simulator builds on the exponential-skip coupon process Kevin sketched in Appendix B of his paper: maintain just 64 empty-cell counters mjm_jmjâ, the running HIP accumulator, and processed element count. Note one essential catch: HIP values cannot be reconstructed from final column counts alone, because HIP is strictly path-dependent on discovery order. As a minimal counterexample at K=16K = 16K=16, hitting column 1 and then column 2 yields 2.0323, whereas hitting column 2 and then column 1 yields 2.0159, even though the final column counts are identical. To be clear, the million-trial Monte Carlo simulator and raw trial outputs were kept locally as an independent verification record rather than checked into the PR.

The reconstructed generators, closed-form constants, and hardened tests have been merged upstream in PR-355.

Writing those unit tests underscored an vital engineering lesson: never write tautological tests. An earlier draft verified the asymptotic constant against a second hardcoded copy inside the test file, and checked confidence bounds only by testing whether they bracketed the point estimate. Simple mutation testing exposed both gaps immediately: changing the production constant to a coarse 0.794024 or zeroing out all 132 confidence-table entries still passed every test. We hardened the merged tests in two ways: the constant test calls production code directly to compare the runtime constant against the closed form, and the confidence-table test asserts strict monotonicity of interval width with kappa while stating its verification limits explicitly in comments. Today, all 23 Huffman tables and 16 permutation tables have bit-exact constructive tests, whereas the Monte Carlo confidence tables clearly document that unit tests do not verify empirical cell values or true coverage.

In a recent development, when reverse-engineering legacy numerical code, the biggest trap is thinking, âall tests pass, so we recovered what the author wrote.â Proving a model reproduces the artifacts is not proving the author coded that model. Throughout code comments and this report, we drew a bright line between parameters uniquely pinned by data and equivalence classes that observations cannot tell apart, leaving six open questions for the community:.

Recent findings suggest that when I first spotted those two orphaned ocamlopt lines while porting CpcSketch back in January, they looked like a dead end. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI, speaks at Microsoft Ignite 2026 in San Francisco, 17 November 2026.
  • Microsoft has released MAI Code 2, an in-house coding model.
  • The company presented it at its Ignite conference in San Francisco on Tuesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI, speaks at Microsoft Ignite 2026 in San Francisco, 17 November 2026.

Microsoft has released MAI Code 2, an in-house coding model. It says the model delivers 98% of the performance of OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol at 40% of the price.

The company presented it at its Ignite conference in San Francisco on Tuesday. Latest models for security and image editing rolled out alongside it.

Against Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5, Microsoft says MAI Code 2 gives 96% of the performance at 5% of the cost. The figures are averages across four coding benchmarks that Microsoft chose.

Both comparisons use a launch price. A footnote to Microsoft AI’s announcement says the cost is shown at a 50% promotional rate. That rate runs until 17 May 2027, GitHub’s pricing page shows. After that, input tokens rise from $0.50 to $1 per million. Output tokens rise from $2.50 to $5 per million.

Sources indicate that MAI Code 2 and a smaller model, MAI Code 2 Flash, are available in GitHub Copilot. Microsoft states Flash matches OpenAI’s GPT-6 Luna at 65% of the price. It matches Anthropic’s Claude Haiku 5.5 at 20%.

Mustafa Suleyman, chief executive of Microsoft AI, led the launch on stage.

“Right now, token spend is going through the roof,” Suleyman mentioned, describing what he hears from CIOs and CFOs.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft indicates both coding models are not yet tuned for harder problems. Those include fundamental science research and very long agentic work.

Microsoft is also building a general-purpose frontier model, Suleyman told Axios. He noted the tech giant has reached state-of-the-art pre-training results. It is also making strong progress in reinforcement learning. He gave no release date.

“My team is building true superintelligence,” Suleyman told Axios.

He gave no target for how much Copilot traffic will move to Microsoft’s own models. He predicted significant adoption.

MAI Cyber 2 Flash, a security model, beats OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, Suleyman noted. It does so at less than 2% of the cost per task. A larger MAI Cyber 2 is in preview inside MDASH, Microsoft’s agentic code scanner.

In a recent development, MAI Image 2.7 is now the top image editing model, Suleyman mentioned. It costs a fifth of what its rivals charge.

Microsoft is also launching MAI Licensed Weights. Trusted customers can take a Microsoft AI model and customise it with their own data. They then run it in their own Azure environment, with help from Microsoft’s Frontier Company team.

Suleyman told Axios the approach would “feel like open source” with more security and control.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into somebody else’s model,” Suleyman said on stage.

AT&T built a custom version of Code 2 Flash. It beats GPT-6.1 Sol at standard 5G network analysis and costs 50 times less, according to Suleyman.

Industry observers note that microsoft still sells OpenAI and Anthropic models. Satya Nadella announced OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 for Microsoft Foundry on the same stage. Earlier, Microsoft’s commercial chief pitched Copilot as cheaper than ChatGPT and Claude.

Microsoft cut back Claude Code licences for its own engineers in May over token costs. In September, Suleyman took on Anthropic over how it trains Claude.

  • First register your details to create a user profile for the hub, then login to access all content within the hub.
  • It has been revealed that IEEE Spectrum Magazine, the flagship publication of the IEEE, explores the development, applications and implications of new technologies.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then demonstrates how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

  • Everful, a San Francisco startup that uses AI agents to source products from factories, has raised a $48.5M Series A, the tech giant announced on Thursday.
  • According to recent reports, retailers and brands usually buy stock through layers of middlemen, long email threads and high minimum orders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

San Francisco startup Everful has raised a $48.5M Series A led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital. Its AI agents find and vet factories and manage orders for retailers and brands, and it indicates it is on track for $100M in annualised revenue by year-end.

Everful, a San Francisco startup that uses AI agents to source products from factories, has raised a $48.5M Series A, the tech giant announced on Thursday. Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital led the round, with existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed taking part.

According to recent reports, retailers and brands usually buy stock through layers of middlemen, long email threads and high minimum orders. Everful’s agents spot trending products, find and vet factories, and handle the messages for each order.

Everful scores each factory on quality using its own inspections, then ships the goods itself. Customers can buy wholesale, dropship or order custom products with low minimums. Quality checks are drawing AI investment too, with Smartex launching AI fabric checks for H&M on Thursday.

“AI lets us turn that team into software,” said co-founder and CEO Sisi Song, referring to the overseas sourcing teams big retailers hire.

Sources indicate that founded in 2024, Everful states it now ships more than 5 million items a month to customers in over 60 countries. It works with more than 30,000 factories and says it is on track for $100M in annualised revenue by year-end. Those figures come from the company and have not been independently confirmed.

In a recent development, song is a former Alibaba executive and Bessemer Venture Partners investor. Co-founder Kevin Han previously sold his AI startup, Orbeus, to Amazon.

The money will fund growth in the US, its biggest market, and Europe. Investors are betting on AI agents across the supply chain: Freehand raised $75M in July to manage tech giant spending, and Plato raised $14.5M to automate wholesale trade.

Cheap cross-border shopping is also under pressure. Shein, which lost its US tariff exemption, is pitching its IPO at under $30B, far below its 2022 valuation.

Making 8-page foldable zines from a single A4 sheet in the browser

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A few months ago, I wrote about how I started giving away zines to my friends, my family, and people at work.
  • If you've never made one, the fold is simple.
  • I fill mine with whatever I feel like printing: photos, poems, or notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A few months ago, I wrote about how I started giving away zines to my friends, my family, and people at work.

If you've never made one, the fold is simple. Take a single A4 sheet of paper, fold it in half three times, open it back up, and cut along the center crease with scissors. Fold the sheet into a cross and close it, and you have an 8-page booklet with no staples or glue.

I fill mine with whatever I feel like printing: photos, poems, or notes.

The part I never liked was laying out the flat sheet on the computer before printing. Because the A4 paper folds back on itself, the pages sit in a strange order and the top row has to be upside down:.

I got tired of rotating pictures and double-checking columns in Photoshop every time I wanted to print a new zine, so I built fanzines.app.

In the browser, you lay out each page right-side up with photos and text. When you export, the app places all 8 panels onto the A4 grid with the top row rotated 180 degrees and generates a 300 DPI PDF. Everything stays local in the browser; no photos are uploaded to a server.

Over the last few days, I rebuilt the editor around the things that kept getting in my way when I sat down to make a zine.

It has been revealed that in the first version, the sidebar listed the 8 pages in a plain two-column grid. It paired the Front Cover with Page 1, Page 2 with Page 3, Page 4 with Page 5, and Page 6 with the Back Cover.

It looked tidy on screen, but it didn't match the physical booklet. When you hold a folded zine, the front cover sits alone on the right. Open it and Page 1 faces Page 2 across the fold, then 3 faces 4, 5 faces 6, and the back cover ends up alone on the left.

The sidebar now groups the page thumbnails into those real spreads, in reading order.

It has been revealed that I also added a Spread view on the canvas. While you're editing Page 1, Page 2 sits beside it at lower opacity so you can check how the two facing pages sit together before printing. Clicking the dimmed page switches straight to editing it.

In a recent development, when I make a photo zine, I usually start with a folder of 8 photos already picked out. Now you can drag the whole batch onto the editor window, and the sidebar highlights which pages will take each photo in reading order before you drop them.

I changed the side panel too. Early on, clicking a photo opened four coordinate inputs (X, Y, Width, Height). I rarely needed to type coordinates; mostly I wanted a photo to fill the page, fit inside the margins, or sit centered. Fill, Fit, and Center now sit at the top of the inspector and in a small toolbar above the selection.

The exact fields are still in a collapsible section at the bottom, now in millimeters (for the 74.25 × 105 mm folded panel) and points for text.

Before downloading the PDF, a Review step highlights the full unfolded A4 sheet with toggles for cut/fold lines and a 5 mm safe margin. Most home printers clip a few millimeters around the edge of an A4 sheet, so the safe margin scales the layout to about 95% to keep the covers intact.

A couple of other additions: the editor now works on phone screens (one page at a time with a thumbnail strip along the bottom), and the site is available in English as well as Spanish. Changing the language keeps your current pages.

You can create your own zine in English or Spanish at fanzines.app.

Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella speaks at Microsoft Ignite 2026 in San Francisco, 17 November 2026.

Industry observers note that office in Copilot is now generally available, according to Microsoft’s Ignite news page. So is Home, which brings Chat and Cowork together in one place.

“But time has come for a true multiplayer form factor,” Nadella stated.

“We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. And in that context, I know we have work to do,” Nadella stated.

“You can simply think of this as an ERP system of AI usage,” Nadella mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that “How can you even trust all this powerful technology? And the reality is, by definition, you can’t,” Nadella mentioned.

“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us,” Nadella stated.

“It’s up to the Nvidia board to decide what happens next,” Nadella mentioned.

“I don’t think the public is getting it wrong,” Nadella mentioned.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Google Quantum AI indicates it has shown contextuality, a quantum property thought to power some algorithms, on up to 105 qubits, in a paper on the cover of Science.
  • According to recent reports, google Quantum AI says a quantum property thought to power some algorithms still holds on up to 105 qubits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A smartphone displaying the Google search start screen.

Google Quantum AI indicates it has shown contextuality, a quantum property thought to power some algorithms, on up to 105 qubits, in a paper on the cover of Science. The tests also expose subtle hardware errors, but the paper does not claim an unconditional advantage over classical computers.

According to recent reports, google Quantum AI says a quantum property thought to power some algorithms still holds on up to 105 qubits. The research, published on Thursday on the cover of Science, tested the property on Google’s superconducting quantum processors.

The property is called contextuality. It means a measurement’s result is not fixed in advance, but depends on which other measurements are made alongside it. Until now, it had mostly been shown in systems of just a few particles.

Sources indicate that in one test, Google’s qubits won a two-player game, the Mermin-Peres magic square, 98.3% of the time. The best possible classical strategy wins only 88.9% of the time. A larger task using 105 qubits also beat classical strategies with limited resources.

Google states the tests double as a sensitive way to catch subtle hardware errors that other benchmarks miss. It says this could help pave the way for uses in chemistry and materials science, though the experiments did not simulate either.

The paper is careful about its limits. It claims there is no unconditional proof that quantum computers beat classical ones in general, and its quantum edge in one game shrank as more qubits joined. The work first appeared as a preprint in December 2025.

Industry observers note that error-free hardware remains the industry’s big goal. Google has mentioned it wants a useful, error-corrected quantum computer by 2029, and Microsoft, which unveiled its Majorana 2 chip in June, has set the same target.

In a recent development, IBM agreed to buy HRL as it highlighted a chip that corrects its own errors, and Nvidia has simulated a 104-qubit error-corrected machine. Investors are piling in too, with Quantinuum raising $1.68B in its IPO in June.

Apple among the companies facing pressure from US senators over ‘nudify’ apps [U: Apple, TTP respond]

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps.
  • Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable users to generate nonconsensual nude images.
  • According to the updated rules, apps that allow users to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details.

Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable users to generate nonconsensual nude images.

According to the updated rules, apps that allow users to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.

Apple also warns that apps used primarily for pornographic content or the objectification of real people may be removed from the App Store without notice.

While definitely well-intended, Apple’s changes came amid growing reports of AI-powered nudify apps, which easily allow users to generate nonconsensual intimate images.

Two months before these changes, Apple removed an app that allowed users to create pornographic deepfakes of real people after WIRED reached out for comment, which in turn came one month after San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove several nudify apps from their app stores.

Apple also removed several apps following investigations by the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), which published reports in January and April revealing that such apps were widely available on the App Store, sometimes even appearing in sponsored search results.

Throughout these investigations, Apple has maintained that nudify apps have always been prohibited under its App Review Guidelines, and that it proactively rejects and removes apps that violate its policies, including those flagged through user reports.

Apple, of course, is not alone in this challenge, with Google facing similar criticism over their availability on the Play Store, and Meta coming under scrutiny for allowing developers to advertise these apps on Facebook and Instagram, as highlighted in the WIRED report mentioned above.

Which brings us to today’s report from The Guardian.

According to The Guardian’s exclusive report, “three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms.”.

A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

The senators, namely Ron Wyden of Oregon, Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Ben Luján of Newly introduced Mexico, claim that in addition to failing to remove these apps, the companies may actually be profiting from their distribution and promotion.

Commenting on the letter, both Google and Meta remarked they prohibit such apps or their promotion and work to detect and remove violations from their platforms, broadly echoing what Apple has repeatedly stated when reached for comment in the past over these same challenges.

However, Wyden’s office argues that simply reaffirming, or in Apple’s case, updating these policies, means little if the companies continue to struggle to enforce them.

Sources indicate that keith Chu, the chief communications adviser and deputy policy director to Wyden, said that clarifying policies is not the same thing as enforcing them. Despite the companies reaffirming the prohibition of these apps, they continue to proliferate across Apple and Google app stores or be promoted in ads on Meta platforms, he added.

In its latest investigation, published just last month, TTP found 135 apps capable of generating nude or pornographic imagery on the App Store and the Play Store, using accounts registered to 13-year-old boys.

Additionally, researchers found that even accounts configured with parental controls were able to download these apps without requiring parental approval.

Despite Apple and Google removing the apps identified in the investigation, The Guardian noted that these apps continued to work on devices where they had already been installed.

Now, Senator Wyden warns that Congress may need to step in if the companies fail to do a better job of cracking down on these apps.

To read The Guardian’s full report, follow this link.

Sources indicate that revision, 8:40 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said:.

In a recent development, “We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for people. A number of the apps in the TTP report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities. We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process — a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch. We previously removed 28 of the apps referenced in this report before it was shared with us and have taken action on the remaining apps found to violate our rules. The report also relies on testing from older software that does not reflect current Apple safety features, including expanded protections for teens and parental controls in Screen Time that give families the ability to block kids and teens from downloading apps rated above their age.”.

Expanding on the safety features mentioned in its statement, Apple noted that teens aged 13 through 17 now have certain protections enabled by default, including web content filters, even if their parents haven’t configured any restrictions, and pointed to ⁠this support article for more information.

The firm added that children under 13 are required to use Child Accounts, and that the report relied on its previous 17+ age rating system, which was replaced last year with a more granular system that includes 13+, 16+, and 18+ ratings.

Sources indicate that just curious. Why doesn't someone from Apple try out the app before approving it, rather than approving it and waiting until people complain? I know there are many thousands of apps on the App store. But given that Apple makes money off most of these apps, it could surely afford to hire a staff charged with reviewing submitted apps to ensure compliance with the App store's guidelines and requirements before making them available in the App store. What am I missing here?

Apple also noted that in its report, TTP counted apps depicting people in swimwear or lingerie, which the manufacturer said does not constitute nudification or, in itself, violate its guidelines.

As for parental controls, Apple explained that, although apps that exceed a child’s configured age restrictions won’t appear in curated App Store sections, they can still be found through search, allowing children to request permission to download them through Ask to Buy. Without parental approval, the download remains blocked.

Industry observers note that apple added that Ask to Buy is supposed to require parental approval even for purchases made using gift card balances, including subscriptions. The manufacturer said that if a purchase didn’t trigger an approval request, that would be unexpected behavior, and that it is investigating further.

According to recent reports, enhancement, November 19, 4:00 p.m. ET: In response to Apple’s statement, TTP director Katie Paul reached out to 9to5Mac with the following comment:.

Apple’s statement on nudify apps sidesteps crucial concerns and leaves out key context. The company says it prohibits nudify apps but doesn’t address how its age rating system for apps contributes to the problem. TTP has shown how Apple relies on information provided by app developers to set age ratings—a self-reporting system that allows many nudify and pornographic apps to be misleadingly labeled a suitable for minors. Apple also continues to talk about removing nudify apps from the App Store, without mentioning that apps that are “removed” continue to be fully functional on people’s phones.

Recent findings suggest that there are many questions about Apple’s policy on nudify apps that the statement fails to address. Apple has adopted a limited definition of “nudify.” The tech giant defines nudify apps as capable of showing someone naked, not stripping them down to a bikini or lingerie. But the company also notes it bans “creepy” and “nonconsensual intimate imagery.” What if an app is used to depict a woman in a bikini without her consent? We have asked Apple to clarify that and have not heard back.

As for Apple’s comment that TTP relied on “older software,” that may refer to the fact that Apple rolled out new child safety features in the fall. Our research was conducted in summer 2026. But many of Apple’s new features pertain to parent-supervised accounts on Apple, which have to be set up by a parent. Apple relies entirely on parents to go out of their way to locate and enable these settings. This raises obvious questions about how many people actually do this.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

JPMorgan Chase indicates hackers got into data held by companies that work for the bank, and that it may include some customers’ names and email addresses. Visa and Mastercard have also confirmed incidents at outside providers.

We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack.

Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.

There is no disruption to our services.

Where appropriate, we will contact affected customers directly and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring.

There is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week.

— Chase (@Chase) November 19, 2026.

According to recent reports, the bank remarked the attackers accessed marketing data held by those vendors. Its own services kept running. It will offer affected customers free credit monitoring where appropriate.

Chase also said the attack has no link to Monday’s outage, which it blamed on a software bug in its own hardware.

A ransomware gang called n0n published the data after a 48-hour deadline passed, Cybernews reported. Its researchers found about 16,000 customer email addresses, Chase account IDs and, in some cases, phone numbers. The file also holds 124 email addresses of bank staff.

Industry observers note that all of the records seem to relate to Chase’s Reserve card, Cybernews stated. The invitation-only Visa card is for wealthy clients, usually with at least $10m in managed assets.

“This association alone makes the leak a lot more sensitive,” stated Aras Nazarovas, a senior security researcher at Cybernews.

Recent findings suggest that the file is only 502KB. It is not clear whether it is a sample or all the gang took. TNW has not independently verified the data.

A Mastercard spokesperson told Business Insider that an outside provider exposed a limited number of email addresses. They belong to a small group of cardholders in one benefit programme. Mastercard said it has contained the exposure.

“There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards,” the spokesperson stated.

Visa said its incident involved a service provider in the Asia Pacific region.

In a recent development, “Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected,” a Visa spokesperson stated.

None of the three companies has named the vendors or remarked how many customers the breach hit.

n0n is a new gang, first tracked in mid-September, according to Cybernews. Last week it claimed to have stolen data from Expedia.

Sources indicate that the leak comes at the end of a week of outages across the US. Wall Street executives and the NSA have reportedly blamed several of them on rushed security patches for flaws that AI found, not on hackers. Earlier this week, attackers also used Optimizely’s testing tool to plant malware on major websites.

Light is one of the biggest triggers for your body clock. A lack of light signals it's time to sleep, while bright lights help you feel alert. It's a reason why many of us (including me) find it easier to wake up in summer, when the sun has naturally risen by the time you're getting out of bed.

In winter, however, dark mornings often lead to sleep inertia. Instead of being slowly woken by the rising sun, you're jolted awake by an alarm screeching in the middle of your sleep cycle.

There are two potential solutions. First, you can shift your wake up until the sun naturally rises. Appealing, but potentially disruptive and on some overcast days, you might never get out of bed.

Second, a sunrise alarm clock. The Hatch Sleep Clock steps up when the sun isn't around. It lights up slowly (over a preset period) meaning when the built-in alarm starts to chime, you've already received key signals that it's time to get going. And instead of blinking awake in darkness, you open your eyes to a well lit room.

Every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an update that addresses one of its users’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days.

As spotted by The Verge, Instagram head Adam Mosseri confirmed today that the app will finally let users edit a Story after publishing.

This means consumers will be able to add stickers and drawings, fix typos or adjust text, and even change the music without having to delete the Story and publish it again, which would mean losing any views it had already received.

The catch is that customers will only have 15 minutes after publishing a Story to make changes by tapping the ellipsis button at the bottom of the screen, and then selecting “Edit story.”.

Here’s Mosseri’s post announcing the news:.

A post shared by Adam Mosseri (@mosseri).

Today’s update is the latest in a series of changes Instagram has made this year to address longstanding user requests.

Recent findings suggest that back in March, the app introduced the ability to reorder photos and videos in a carousel after publishing. In April, it added an option to edit comments (also within 15 minutes of posting), and in June, it began letting customers manually rearrange posts on their profile grid.

More recently, Instagram also brought its free Edits video editor to the Mac, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, and 4K exports.

Oil and gas exploration and production company ConocoPhillips is this week's first dividend pick. With a dividend of 84 cents per share (annualized dividend of $3.36 per share), COP offers a dividend yield of 3%. The company is scheduled to announce its second-quarter results on Aug. 6.

Despite the pressure on oil prices from an increase in OPEC production quota, the analyst finds ConocoPhillips and Shell stocks appealing as the earnings season approaches.
