#50796. Scout Motors Is Using AI Earpieces to Train Factory Workers

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (978 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Scout Motors Is Using AI Earpieces to Train Factory Workers

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “AI training” usually refers to instilling artificial intelligence with human knowledge.
  • Sources indicate that CEO Scott Keogh spoke with CNET during a reporters roundtable at Scout’s still-under-construction factory in Blythewood, South Carolina.
  • Keogh described the approach as starting from the work itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“AI training” usually refers to instilling artificial intelligence with human knowledge. Scout Motors claims it’s been doing the opposite: using AI tools to help hire, onboard and train factory workers, including an AI assistant in an earpiece that guides trainees through tasks as they perform them.

Sources indicate that CEO Scott Keogh spoke with CNET during a reporters roundtable at Scout’s still-under-construction factory in Blythewood, South Carolina. Keogh said that rather than “sitting new hires down with an instructional binder and a test,” workers are getting AI-driven, hands-on experience early in a push to make the training more efficient and effective. Meanwhile, the automaker can collect and feed training data back into the system to fine-tune its hiring, training and placement processes.

Keogh described the approach as starting from the work itself. Manufacturing, he stated, can be broken down into a handful of fundamental tasks, and the AI system is built to teach each one. He offered parts picking as the simplest example: A worker walks to 12 boxes, pulls 12 parts, confirms they’re in the right sequence and checks them for defects. The AI in the earpiece can guide the worker through that sequence, providing real-time, adaptable instructions.

“We can train that within minutes,” Keogh remarked. “A worker repeats the cycle about 15 times, getting faster and better each pass, and then moves down the task line to the next skill.”.

To my ears, that doesn’t sound like the sort of task you’d need an AI system to help with and, to some extent, Scout’s executives agreed.

However, the automaker’s representatives argued that the new method is far more productive than traditional classroom training — with increasing benefits as the trained tasks and concepts become more complex. Keogh also linked the speed at which the company has seen its newest factory hires become productive with how promptly Scout can ramp up the factory itself.

Scout execs say AI also plays a role in the hiring and onboarding before training begins. Todd Johnson, vice president of manufacturing, remarked the team feeds latest hires’ backgrounds into an AI system, which suggests where each person might fit best: A former forklift driver might be steered toward logistics, someone with no final assembly experience might do better in the body shop and a person with paint shop experience could be placed as a painter.

Industry observers note that again, that sounded a lot like common sense to me. Isn’t that how people were hired before AI? According to Scout Motors’ leadership, the algorithm can potentially identify less obvious connections between skills and tasks that a human might miss, expanding access to jobs for applicants who may not have received traditional manufacturing training, which is key because Scout’s upcoming plant is located in an area that doesn’t have a large pool of local dyed-in-the-wool traditional automotive workers.

In a recent development, to fill the over 4,000 roles that factory will need to reach full speed ahead by 2028, the automaker says it’s hiring from a national pool of applicants. However, executives told me that using AI to consider nontraditional factory workers — citing one hire who worked at the DMV — will allow Scout to identify and place more local applicants and bring fresh ideas to the factory floor.

Ryan Decker, vice president of strategy and brand, called Scout’s AI-forward approach to placement and training “a passion project for the organization.” Decker told CNET that Scout’s training AI can tailor instruction to each person rather than delivering the same material to a room of 10 people over 10 days. People learn differently, he noted, with different language skills and levels of technical depth.

Decker also said the system is bidirectional. The AI can learn from how each group responds to the training and use that information to modify instruction for the next cohort. Decker thinks that each subsequent batch of workers will be “1% better,” and that after 1,000 repetitions, he expects the AI to be “dialed in and know how to provide information to the people in the most productive way possible.”.

Scout says it’s also exploring vision-based AI training, in which the trainee is guided via augmented reality glasses, as the next evolution of the technology. The automaker is also looking to eventually expand the tech for do-it-yourself use by owners at home. I imagine a future where owners can use an Apple Vision Pro or similar device — which would be a pricey investment — to guide themselves through installing a roof rack or performing routine maintenance.

In practice, the next step, according to Scout’s execs, is to scale its AI learning tools beyond the training room and into the actual factory and service centers, where the automaker believes the tech can continue to improve on-the-floor productivity and guide its workers as they advance through their careers.

Decker states the AI can ingest and organize decades of institutional knowledge, making it accessible to workers during and beyond the training process. Scout has been feeding the AI equipment manuals and manufacturing documentation spanning multiple decades, disciplines and countries — what Decker called “hundreds of years of accumulated enterprise know-how” — which the AI earpiece can surface in real time, something he noted was near impossible to do before in a world of binders and PDFs.

Scout’s AI-fueled “passion project” arrives amid broader tensions across industries affected by artificial intelligence. Companies are eager for the efficiencies AI promises, while workers worry the same technology could eventually cost them their jobs. Scout’s executives didn’t address that concern directly in this exchange. Keogh framed the payoff in terms of speed — how promptly a new hire can be made productive — leaving the wider workforce conversation for another time.

Editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Scout Motors. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that have you been using the newly introduced Siri AI? If so, how much? I’ve been turning to it a lot since the release of iOS 27. Well, how we use it — and how often — will soon depend on how much we pay for an iCloud+ plan.

Also: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers.

Apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits. Increased limits would be granted based on your iCloud+ subscription. Now the company has revealed how much it will cost you and when the limits will begin.

Industry observers note that “Starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for users with a supported device set to a supported language,” Apple stated on a support page updated November 16. “Some features rely on powerful server models and have limits where increased access is available with eligible iCloud+ looks, starting with the 27.3 release.”.

iOS 27.3 is expected to launch in early December, so that’s when the daily usage limits will kick in.

At that point, people with no paid iCloud+ plan and even those with the $0.99-per-month 50 GB plan will be the most limited, with Apple saying only that they’ll face a “Standard Device Limit.”.

What is a standard limit? That depends not just on how many times you tap into Siri per day but on what tasks you assign it. Basic Siri commands, such as setting timers and alarms or sending standard text messages, will remain free and unlimited.

It has been revealed that also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

Recent findings suggest that advanced Siri and Apple Intelligence tasks will bump into the usage limits. These include the following, according to Apple:.

One positive here is that the limits are per device not per account. That means you can use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence with the same account across your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro without fear of chewing up too much of your quota.

This all sounds like a way for Apple to steer people to more expensive iCloud+ accounts. But the limits are in place for a key reason. Basic commands are processed on your device, so they don’t require the use of Apple servers. More advanced tasks are processed using server-side AI models, which can feel the strain if too many people access them all at once.

Also: What you’ll pay for AI agents will be wildly variable and unpredictable.

In a recent development, how will you know if you use up your daily allotment and what happens then? You’ll receive a notification if you hit your limit for a particular feature category. Otherwise, Apple is undoubtedly hoping that people who continually run into limits will upgrade to a pricier iCloud+ proposal.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, at Scout Motors’ South Carolina Production Center, the automaker’s very first electrified trucks and SUVs are being welded, painted and assembled.
  • After a period of slow sales, American interest in electric vehicles and hybrids is on the rise, driven by high fuel costs and the steady growth of EV charging infrastructure in 2026.
  • I donned my hardhat, steel-toe caps and high-vis vest to get an early look inside the plant.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, at Scout Motors’ South Carolina Production Center, the automaker’s very first electrified trucks and SUVs are being welded, painted and assembled. The revived American automaker has begun the first validation builds of its upcoming Terra pickup truck and Traveler SUV at the Blythewood plant, but hold your electric horses — final production and customer deliveries are still a little over a year away.

After a period of slow sales, American interest in electric vehicles and hybrids is on the rise, driven by high fuel costs and the steady growth of EV charging infrastructure in 2026. Scout, with its battery-electric and gasoline range-extended powertrains, could have both of those bases covered when it arrives to compete in America’s most popular vehicle classes (trucks and SUVs) in 2028. It’s worth keeping an eye on Scout as it inches toward production.

I donned my hardhat, steel-toe caps and high-vis vest to get an early look inside the plant.

The Volkswagen Group revived the Scout Motors brand (formerly International Scout) in 2022, and in 2024, the public got its first look at the Terra and Traveler concepts. The two were initially revealed as full-electric models with the option to add Scout’s Harvester onboard gasoline generator to boost the range.

However, demand for the extended-range EV configuration was overwhelming — roughly 87% of the 160,000-plus reservation holders selected the Harvester spec over the all-electric version — and Scout pivoted to delivering the EREV first, then following up with the pure battery-electric model later in production.

Both models are expected to start under $60,000, though Scout has not yet confirmed the exact price difference between the Harvester and pure BEV trims.

Industry observers note that in early 2024, the automaker broke ground on the Blythewood Production Center, pledging to invest more than $2 billion in the plant and create more than 4,000 local jobs. A year later, Scout announced intends to add a $300 million supplier park to the complex, supporting around 1,000 on-site jobs at parts suppliers.

Industry observers note that today, construction is mostly complete. (Executives told me it’s about 80% to 95% done, depending on how you measure it.) The walls are up, much of the equipment is in place, and the first movement toward full production of the brand’s extended-range EV and, eventually, battery electric trucks and SUVs has begun.

Scout’s manufacturing and production teams have begun building the first validation builds — early-stage preproduction vehicles that allow factory planners to dial in vehicle quality, confirm the accuracy of the engineering and hone the efficiency of the manufacturing and assembly lines.

These aren’t complete vehicles by any stretch, being pulled from the line at various points to check and double-check that the fresh factory equipment functions properly and that the right parts arrive when and where they’re needed. Executives warned me that, at this point, there would still be inconsistencies as they dial in panel gaps, welds and the application of various coatings, but that Scout expects the process to be dialed in by the time full production starts in late 2027.

I was able to get up close to these validation vehicles, checking out a body-in-white bare chassis in the body shop, seeing various stages of coatings applied to bare metal, and watching workers complete calibration and alignment of lights and sensors in the final assembly area.

Recent findings suggest that along the way, Scout told me that more than 160 individual parts must come together to form the vehicle’s chassis, a process supported by more than 750 robots and 5,000 weld points. Once up to speed, the factory body shop is designed to produce around 40 vehicles per hour, with pickups and SUVs sharing the same line.

Recent findings suggest that however, while I saw the robotic welding arms and paint sprayers performing their motions to apply color, no vehicles were actually moving through the assembly line. This early in the process, the automaker doesn’t need a continuous flow of validation vehicles, and many of the factory areas — such as the supplier park that will provide the batteries, electric motors and modified VW Group four-cylinder engines for Harvester models — are still under construction.

Additionally, the validation process gives workers hands-on experience, rather than having them learn from mistakes on cars that will reach customers or being confined to a classroom.

It has been revealed that as more parts of the factory complete construction and come online, the validation process will encompass more of the vehicle’s construction until the automaker is ready to start building full customer vehicles. Todd Johnson, Scout’s vice president of manufacturing, tells me that validation will continue into 2027 through multiple preproduction phases starting with the Traveler SUV.

The automaker expects the first customer deliveries of the Traveler Harvester to begin in early 2028, followed by the Terra Harvester and, eventually, fully electric versions of both.

It has been revealed that editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Scout Motors. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

Google’s Gemini can now turn your notes and other sources in your Gemini Notebook (previously called NotebookLM) into interactive pages or sites to help you better process complicated information.

In a recent development, complete with flashcards, dashboards, and colorful panels, the sites make it easier to study and understand intricate concepts. I tested the feature, confirmed Tuesday, to see how efficient it is at creating a navigable site that is actually helpful and stays loyal to sources.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s latest Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector in my tests.

Because Notebooks are built with the sources you provide, like textbooks, files, or notes, the sites are created with the data that is in your Gemini Notebook. Notebook has three tabs: Sources, Chat, and Studio. The site option is in the Studio tab, listed under what you can create.

If you’re taking a college class, you could put all the information you need to prepare for a test and use the interactive site as a study guide that you can share with others.

To test this, I gave Notebook the following prompt:.

“Make me a site that visually explains how cellular respiration works, breaking down each stage with interactive diagrams and self-check flashcards.”.

Since I’m not in a class that would give me those study materials, I gave Gemini online sources to use for this. Gemini cited the sources in my notebook, then spent a few minutes creating the interactive site. Gemini will give you a quick enhancement when it’s done, including a summary of the source information as it pertains to your request and instructions on where to find the site.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

As promised, my cellular respiration notes were complete and organized on an interactive, visually appealing site that was easy to navigate. The coolest feature on the site was the flashcards, which you can hover over to see which ones you’ve studied.

According to recent reports, the interactive site feature is now available to Gemini Notebook people and will soon come to the mobile app. As someone who knows very little about coding, I was pretty satisfied to see the information Gemini put together presented in explorable, easy-to-understand tabs on a site.

#50788. Ford Designed Its Fathom EV Battery Pack to Bend in a Crash, for Safety

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1159 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Ford Designed Its Fathom EV Battery Pack to Bend in a Crash, for Safety

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1159 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ford’s upcoming LFP battery pack isn’t a fragile electric car component that needs protection.
  • According to recent reports, conventional wisdom views an EV battery as a potentially explosive component that, if damaged, can cause catastrophic failure and hours-long fires that are difficult to extinguish.
  • So the anxiety is well founded, even if, statistically, EVs are generally as safe as (if not safer than) internal combustion engine vehicles in crash testing and far less likely to catch fire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ford’s upcoming LFP battery pack isn’t a fragile electric car component that needs protection. During my visit this week to the automaker’s newly operational battery plant, engineers proudly showed me a video of the battery being crash-tested, the shell and the prismatic cells within bending violently under the force. My jaw practically hit the floor.

According to recent reports, conventional wisdom views an EV battery as a potentially explosive component that, if damaged, can cause catastrophic failure and hours-long fires that are difficult to extinguish. Years of lithium-ion batteries in phones, tablets and laptops taught us that and it’s largely held true for electric cars as well.

So the anxiety is well founded, even if, statistically, EVs are generally as safe as (if not safer than) internal combustion engine vehicles in crash testing and far less likely to catch fire.

It has been revealed that ford dropped that bombshell of a video on me at the end of my tour of its Blue Oval Battery Park outside Marshall, Michigan. However, I was barred from recording or photographing the footage.

The design team’s mantra was “don’t assume a cell must never deform.” For the upcoming Fathom and Ford’s Universal EV platform, or UEV, the pack is designed to carry up to 40% of side-impact forces and is treated as part of the vehicle’s crash structure. The company’s leadership and engineers are confident that the EV won’t catch fire or explode despite the bent cells.

In a recent development, “Traditionally the battery is thought of as payload, a fragile jewel you must protect,” remarked Vladimir Bogachuk, chief engineer for advanced vehicle structure architecture at Ford. That approach, he said, means heavy bracing and protective structures around the pack. “The battery is not a jewel you must protect,” he said.

Bogachuk (along with every other Ford engineer and executive I spoke with that day) takes a less-is-more stance on the new EV platform. “The best part is no part,” he told me, “and if you have to have a part, it’s pretty much got to serve multiple functions.” And so the engineers set out to remove unnecessary armor and build a battery that serves double duty as an energy reservoir and crash structure.

Sources indicate that without that extra protection, the resulting EV can be lighter and more efficient, with improved driving dynamics. The UEV pack is deeply integrated into the vehicle’s structure: Its top lid is the cabin floor, and the seats bolt directly onto it. The bottom of the pack is the EV’s underbody. A service door beneath the Fathom’s rear seats will provide access to the charging and power electronics for service without the need to drop the pack.

It has been revealed that the crash videos showed deformation that would scare me on an older EV, but when I stopped to think, it wasn’t much different from what I’ve seen in conventional car side-impact crash tests. Ford states an impact strong enough to deform the battery would also deform the chassis of a conventional vehicle or traditional EV, so the vehicle would likely be totaled anyway. More importantly, the engineers say the driver would be safe from thermal runaway and fire.

When asked, Ford’s engineers said they don’t believe in a “right chemistry” for every electric vehicle. The UEV platform’s LFP — short for lithium iron phosphate — chemistry, prismatic cells and “jelly roll” construction were chosen for low manufacturing cost, resistance to temperature extremes, suitability for bidirectional energy use and the ability to deform while remaining inert under designed loads and forces.

Other automakers have floated solid-state batteries as a potential solution to battery safety and energy density, but the technology isn’t ready for use in production cars — at least not at the scale and price that Ford needs for the reasonably priced Fathom.

Ford hasn’t stated the LFP pack’s energy capacity, the cell capacity or the number of cells the Fathom’s pack will comprise. Based on a cutaway displayed during my tour, I estimate 90 to 108 individual prismatic cells. The aluminum prismatic cans that enclose the cathode-anode “jelly roll” battery provide structural support and aid thermal dissipation throughout the larger pack.

Wes Thibault, chief engineer for global energy storage systems, described the rigorous validation that the cells and packs underwent to reach the point where they can be trusted to bend like a taco. He told me that Ford has “a dedicated abuse-testing team” integrated with battery design and engineering at every level and stage of the manufacturing process, searching for edge cases and probing the limits of what the chemistry, the cells and full production-spec battery packs can take, from withstanding over 150,000 miles of simulated daily driving to remaining safe and inert in a crash. Along the way, CT scans of the cells offered an inside look at the jelly roll and how it was responding.

Ford’s testing covers structural integrity and load-bearing capability, heat soak from minus 40 to 60 degrees Celsius, IP67 water resistance and humidity cycling, and high-charge and high-discharge tests. For multiaxis vibration, the battery, seats and brackets are strapped to what I can describe only as a giant mechanical bull that shakes the hardware through roll, pitch, yaw and multiple harmonic frequencies. Ford can combine multiple factors in a single test, such as a high-humidity heat soak under vibration during high discharge.

Once the first batch of UEV vehicles are on the road, Ford says it’ll be able to capture real-world data from the fleet to further fine-tune its validation methods for future generations of EVs.

Given how well the first model year of Ford’s Mustang Mach-E‘s batteries have held up after six years and thousands of real-world miles, it’s clear the automaker knows a thing or two about building a reliable battery.

That mentioned, the UEV platform’s LFP chemistry and construction are very different from those of the earlier generation, and the automaker is asking much, much more of the pack than just holding and discharging energy. It’s asking the pack to actively protect the souls onboard in the event of a crash. Testing to failure early and learning from those mistakes swiftly is something the engineers I spoke to seem to take very seriously.

This bold, out-of-the-box approach to how the automaker thinks about battery fragility — protecting the souls onboard rather than the “jewel” that is the battery from a potential crash at the end of the vehicle’s life — comes with the promise of more range and efficiency, less weight and more driving fun over the vehicle’s lifetime.

I’m ready to believe. I want EV batteries to be safer and less scary. That promise depends heavily on whether the Fathom’s UEV battery pack is as safe as Ford says it is when it reaches driveways and dealerships in late 2027.

Editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Ford. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the past week has been hard on Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 19, 2026 at 4:15PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

According to recent reports, the past week has been hard on Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%). The semiconductor leader had to separate from its co-founder and now-former CEO, Jensen Huang, after he was embroiled in a scandal involving alleged extramarital affairs, including with a woman believed to be a Chinese intelligence asset. Colette Kress, who remains CFO, has stepped up as interim CEO, leading the company through its first quarterly patch since Huang's departure.

Sources indicate that and what an revision it was. Nvidia once again crushed expectations, but that wasn't enough to jolt the stock, which remains down significantly since it reached a upcoming all-time high in early October. Is Nvidia a generational buying opportunity at current levels?

Death, taxes, and Nvidia's financial results coming in above analysts' projections seem to be the only certain things these days. In the third quarter of its fiscal year 2027, which ended on Oct. 25, the tech giant's revenue came in at $115.8 billion, up 103% compared to the year-ago period. Data center revenue grew 110% year over year to $107.6 billion.

In a recent development, nvidia's non-GAAP gross margin was 74.9%, compared to the 73.5% reported in the prior-year quarter. The semiconductor specialist's non-GAAP operating income was $77.9 billion, rising 116% year over year, while its non-GAAP earnings per share were $2.68, up 111% year over year.

The fact that profits are growing faster than revenue is a strong sign for Nvidia, given the industry's increasing competitiveness. While some investors worry that competition from custom AI chips will erode the company's pricing power in the GPU (graphics processing unit) market, as hyperscalers and other corporations increasingly opt for these custom chips, it seems, at least, that this hasn't happened yet. Improving margins are a sign that Nvidia maintains strong pricing power.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's free cash flow for the period was $43.8 billion, rising 98% year over year. The company also posted excellent guidance. Nvidia expects $130 billion in revenue (at the midpoint) for its fourth quarter. That would represent a 91% year-over-year increase.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

Industry observers note that of course, Nvidia's financial results and guidance were only part of the story. The market wants to know how the firm's efforts to replace Huang are going. Nvidia noted it isn't interested in bringing back Huang, despite many people, both inside and outside the company, calling for his reinstatement. And it is actively looking for a replacement, although nobody knows when Nvidia will find someone to step into the CEO role permanently. In my opinion, that's both good and bad.

It's bad because the longer this search drags on, the more uncertainty it could add to the firm's prospects. But it's good because replacing a CEO as effective as Huang isn't an easy task, and the company's board is rightfully taking the time it needs to do so, or so it seems. In the meantime, several factors highlight just how massive an opportunity Nvidia could still tap into, even as it faces a more stringent regulatory environment.

During the recent U.S. midterm elections, voters elected many lawmakers and politicians across various states who had promised to be stricter on the AI industry. This may result in delayed permits and slower data center build-outs. However, Nvidia expects a great year ahead. The organization raised its guidance for the fiscal year 2028, which covers most of the calendar year 2027.

The organization now expects revenue to grow 75% in fiscal year 2028, up from its previous projection of 70% -- and that's after also raising its guidance for its current fiscal year. If we assume Nvidia's fourth-quarter revenue lands at the midpoint, it could generate $423.7 billion this fiscal year and $741.4 billion next year, based on its projected 75% growth rate.

So, given its current market cap of $3.8 trillion, Nvidia is trading at 5.1x estimated fiscal year 2028 revenue -- that's more than fair for a firm growing as fast as it is, in my view. However, the CEO search does introduce some uncertainty. And we still have to account for the risk of margin erosion as industry competition intensifies. So, what's the verdict?

Nvidia looks like a buy at current levels, but it's hardly a once-in-a-decade buying opportunity. Still, investors who purchase the manufacturer's shares today could see strong returns over the medium term.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you haven't updated your Nvidia drivers recently, you may want to hold off. A newly discovered bug apparently can damage your PC by writing excessive amounts of data to solid-state drives (SSDs).

The bug was found in the two most recent Nvidia GPU driver updates — specifically 621.14 and 621.24 — for the Nvidia GeForce Game Ready Driver. The 621.24 patch was released on November 12.

The bug was discovered by TroubleGrid who reported that the bug causes the NVDisplay.Container.exe to write (save data) far too much information to an Nvidia log file that can degrade the SSD. It can result in as much as 30GB per hour.

According to recent reports, the executable already wrote log files before the updates but not that much. SSDs typically take years to degrade, but the excessive data written by this bug can speed up the process causing stuttering and mouse lag.

Sources indicate that on Reddit, I've seen a few posts about the bug with owners complaining that this is why you never revision. "By principle I never ever update my drivers unless there are feature inclusions for let's say a latest game I bought," one Redditor noted.

Plenty of others agreed with that sentiment, and I'm inclined to say they're correct here.

The other half of the comments split between blaming AI-written code. Before his ouster, CEO Jensen Huang was pushing for Nvidia engineers to use more AI-generated code via chatbots and agents.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

It has been revealed that or they were of the belief that Nvidia is purposely killing drives to force customers to pay more for latest ones. Several called out Sam Altman and his recent claim that laptop RAM is a "terrible" allocation of a scarce resource.

"I honestly would not be surprised if they are doing this on purpose to kill our NVMe's," wrote a poster.

If we were to put blame on something, at this point, I'd say its AI-fueled incompetence, not AI-fueled greed, though that has led to mentioned stupidity.

The easiest fix is to rollback your graphics card driver to version 621.01, which is the last known patch to lack this bug.

It has been revealed that troubleGrid listed a manual fix that requires you to set the Nvidia Display Container LS service to manual. Though it'll cost you. Basically, this can disable the Nvidia Control Panel and Nvidia App, meaning G-Sync color settings, display scaling, resolution overrides and more will not rock. "Do not disable the service outright if you use G-SYNC or a custom colour profile," the report warns.

Sources indicate that if you need a temporary fix, you can stop the service, delete the log file and start again. However, the file will return and continue to grow in size.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI.
  • Also: I checked Gemini’s upcoming Memory summary to see what it knew about me.
  • Industry observers note that in a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI. But for people with privacy concerns, the only way to opt out of this was to delete your entire chat history. Now, Google is overhauling the process to eliminate that drawback.

Also: I checked Gemini’s upcoming Memory summary to see what it knew about me.

Industry observers note that in a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Right now, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

To correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two upcoming settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google stated in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

Recent findings suggest that here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both new settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

Almost all AIs include a setting for model training that you typically have to manually disable if you’re concerned about your privacy. But most let you opt out without turning off your chat history.

ChatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”.

Also: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027.

Recent findings suggest that in all those cases, you still retain access to your conversation history. In contrast, Google has been the only AI player among the majors to impose a restriction for those who want to opt out of AI training. Based on past actions, Google has often earned a reputation for being privacy-unfriendly. I’m glad to see the firm take this step in the right direction.

On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 patch for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of new features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

Also: Googlebooks? The best laptop for Android users is something else.

Here are the five new Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

Sources indicate that if you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome update adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly.

When you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

It has been revealed that this auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

The Chrome update allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a new window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.).

You can now save individual Chrome Settings subpages as direct web addresses that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly (for example, chrome://settings/privacy), meaning you won’t have to go digging around in menus to change your preferences anymore. You can navigate between these Settings subpages with the Back and Forward buttons.

Industry observers note that the system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

Recent findings suggest that also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast.

Outside of these upcoming features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the fresh features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually upgrade by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with new Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising.

It has been revealed that if the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the revision, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

Canva Has a Newly introduced Kill Switch for AI: ‘We Know AI Doesn’t Suit Every Task’

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (360 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it’s a great day for designers who hate AI.
  • The settings are available now for free and paying users globally, except for those in India, the Philippines and Indonesia.
  • It has been revealed that to turn off Canva’s AI, go to your Profile > Settings > Preferences and toggle Enable generative AI features on or off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it’s a great day for designers who hate AI. Canva, the online design and publishing platform, declared on Thursday that it’s introducing two upcoming settings to opt out of seeing and using AI tools. One lets you turn off AI tools in Canva, and the other lets you filter out AI-created content from Canva’s library of templates and other elements.

The settings are available now for free and paying users globally, except for those in India, the Philippines and Indonesia. Canva administrators for business and team prepares can enable the two new settings for their entire organization.

It has been revealed that to turn off Canva’s AI, go to your Profile > Settings > Preferences and toggle Enable generative AI features on or off. To filter out AI in your Canva library, go to Profile > Your account > AI personalization and enable the feature that states show less AI-generated content.

It’s hard not to compare Canva’s new opt-out features to Adobe, which spent all of last week at Adobe Max trying to convince creative professionals to embrace its AI tools. Adobe’s chief technology officer told CNET that he thought the problem was slop, not AI.

Industry observers note that as criticisms of AI mount, it’s smart, albeit rare, to see a tech company give its people a definitive, one-click solution to filter out AI tools. We will have to put Canva’s settings to the test to see how effectively they work, though.

Industry observers note that if you do want to use AI, Canva has no shortage. Its magic layers tool lets you break apart an AI-generated image into editable layers, a hugely helpful capability for fixing errors and customizing content. Its foundational models, along with other third-party models, can help you generate latest image, video and audio content. Outside of graphic design, Canva has added AI tools for spreadsheet, document and presentation work over the past year. And like every other tech company, Canva says it plans to continue investing in AI.

For more, check out our guides to muting Meta AI and disabling Google’s AI on your Pixel.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov.
  • It has been revealed that google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini.
  • To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

It has been revealed that google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

Sources indicate that if you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that claims “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.).

Industry observers note that A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get customers familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

According to recent reports, first, you can now share any Skill with other people. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

Industry observers note that when a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

Additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and enhancement in real time, Google states. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.

iPhone Duo, One Month Later: I’m Not Ready to End the Love Affair

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that one month after getting the iPhone Duo, I’ve stuck to my commitment to keep using it even after publishing my review.
  • Recent findings suggest that apple’s debut foldable has proven to be a practical everyday device, whether I’m streaming movies, texting or getting work done.
  • According to recent reports, still, there have been times when I’ve reached for the iPhone 18 Pro Max instead for its more advanced camera system, as well as its familiar, straightforward design.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that one month after getting the iPhone Duo, I’ve stuck to my commitment to keep using it even after publishing my review. Well, mostly.

Recent findings suggest that apple’s debut foldable has proven to be a practical everyday device, whether I’m streaming movies, texting or getting work done. I’ve grown so accustomed to using it that I sometimes forget how much attention it draws when I pull it out of my pocket, especially given its limited availability and lengthy preorder windows – not to mention its sky-high $1,999 starting price.

According to recent reports, still, there have been times when I’ve reached for the iPhone 18 Pro Max instead for its more advanced camera system, as well as its familiar, straightforward design. The Duo’s cameras pull their weight with casual photography, but while filming social content at F1’s US Grand Prix and chatting with filmmakers at an SFFilm screening, I couldn’t resist going for the best cameras at my disposal on the Pro Max. There are times a conventional slab phone just does the trick – without all the frills and novelty of a folding one.

That hasn’t stopped me from keeping the Duo as my primary device. It’s an enjoyable phone to use, with its compact, palm-sized build and spacious inner display. Plus, as CNET’s ongoing folding test demonstrates, it has a durable build that ensures I can fold and unfold it to my heart’s content.

And if I’m being honest, I kind of love how much of a statement piece it’s become.

Industry observers note that the Duo’s versatility has really shown its appeal the more I live with it. I find myself using the 5.4-inch cover screen and 7.6-inch inner display pretty equally, demonstrating the practicality of each.

Sources indicate that when I’m on the move, the cover screen suffices for sending texts, responding to emails and checking notifications. Lounging around at home, I’m more inclined to use the larger inner display to endlessly scroll through Instagram or binge YouTube videos.

Recent findings suggest that the matte inner display remains one of my favorite elements. It reduces the appearance of the crease as well as glare, making it easier to see content even outdoors. Yes, the coating can dim the vibrant colors in images and videos, even with the screen’s 3,000-nit peak brightness, and smudges become prominent. But I can live with both of those drawbacks, and a microfiber cloth fixes the latter.

Apple’s phone-tablet hybrid came in clutch when I was on a recent flight and didn’t want to pull out my laptop. Instead, I used the Duo’s split-screen mode to place the Notes app on one half of the screen and an informational video on the other so I could promptly jot down the main points. The Duo has also become my gym buddy; I prop it open on the treadmill so I can watch Magpie Murders on a tablet-like display, then fold it up and toss it in my pocket when I’m done.

It has been revealed that apple Pencil support really helps the Duo feel like a mini iPad, and the matte coating on the inner display adds a satisfying resistance that more closely emulates the feel of writing on paper than a glossy surface. It gives jotting down notes, highlighting book passages and marking up documents a more tactile feel. I’m not much of a doodler, but I imagine that’s fun, too.

The Apple Pencil can magnetically attach to the outer surface of the hinge, though it definitely sticks out, so there’s not really a practical, secure way to carry it around with the Duo (at least not that Apple has shared, but case-makers are sure to cook up a solution). I’m glad the stylus also works on the Duo’s cover screen, though the smaller size and glossy display make that experience slightly less satisfying.

In a recent development, the number of apps optimized for the Duo at launch was relatively small, but it’s steadily increased. I gasped aloud on the train platform one morning while sending an email, realizing Gmail had finally been adapted for the Duo. It’s refreshing to see apps that feel intentional and fill the screen, rather than being awkwardly letterboxed.

Sources indicate that apple noted in early November that more than 100,000 apps built for the iPhone Duo were live in the App Store. A week later, that number ballooned to over 200,000 apps. So despite a rather slow start, virtually all apps I regularly use now work seamlessly on Apple’s foldable.

One of my favorite apps on the Duo is Instagram’s Edits. When holding the phone open in landscape orientation, I can view the video timeline and make edits on the right side of the screen while seeing a preview of the video on the left. Rotated to portrait orientation, the layout resembles the interface on a traditional smartphone, but on a larger scale, which is helpful especially for making smaller tweaks.

It’s great to see more apps that don’t just expand to the larger screen, but make meaningful use of the Duo’s design.

As I found during my review, the Duo’s battery life has been pretty good. It consistently lasts through the day, even as I hop between displays. I usually charge my phone at night, but even if I don’t, I know I’ll have some remaining battery in the morning.

For instance, one day I started at 6:30 a.m. with a full battery. After my usual routine of checking emails, texting, scrolling through social media and browsing YouTube throughout the day, my battery was at 55% by 9:12 p.m. The next morning, I woke up with 48% battery, and that charge lasted through a similar routine, along with phone calls, texting and music and video streaming, before the battery finally died at 7:30 p.m.

The Duo has yet to give me a reason to stress about its battery life.

I will acknowledge I’m a tad pretentious when it comes to smartphone cameras. But if I’m documenting an event or photographing my fancy tea sets, I want the best cameras I can get. Unlike the Duo, iPhone 18 Pro models have a telephoto camera, more advanced optical zoom capabilities and larger main-camera sensors.

According to recent reports, most of the time, the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras do the trick just fine. Colors are vivid, details are sharp and images are bright. Videos look good, too, though the 18 Pro Max does a noticeably better job with nighttime footage, which can look more muddy on the Duo. Digital video on the Duo also tops out at 6x, versus 24x on the Pros. Most of the time, though, I’m quite content with what I capture with the Duo’s cameras.

As I noted in my review, the under-display FaceTime camera on the inner screen isn’t great, but I never really take selfies using that camera. It feels much more natural to use the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen, which serves up sharp photos every time.

The cover screen selfie camera plays a critical role in an patch that makes using the Duo even more seamless. In its latest iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple added an option to unlock the iPhone Duo using the front camera.

In a recent development, in the absence of Face ID, which I have felt rather painfully, this has been a solid workaround, even if it’s not as secure as Apple’s biometric facial recognition and authentication system. You’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode when using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and to unlock the phone after leaving it alone for around 45 minutes. But a win is a win. (You can also unlock the Duo using an Apple Watch, but I don’t have one.).

In a recent development, I’ll admit I still feel a little bashful when pulling out the Duo because of how much attention it drums up, despite being far from the first foldable phone. But its limited availability and hype paired with the unique design make it eye-catching, for better or worse. Using the Duo has led to some fun conversations, whether it’s with a sales associate as I pay for a pastry or with Project Hail Mary directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, who spotted the phone in my hand during an interview and geeked out over it. That’s been a fun side effect of using Apple’s first foldable in my everyday life.

In a recent development, I’ve been living dangerously without a case; I don’t want anything to detract from the phone’s sleek feel. This is one of those “do as I say, not as I do” moments, as I’d recommend slapping a case on a phone that costs nearly $2,000. I did put a tempered glass screen protector on the cover display to guard against scratches. I can feel its edge against the otherwise flush surface of the phone when I hold it open, but aesthetic sacrifices must be made.

Sources indicate that the Duo isn’t perfect, even if I love using this phone. After holding Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, the iPhone Duo can feel slightly chunky. The Z Fold 8 measures 4.5mm thick when open and 9.7mm when closed. Meanwhile, the Duo is 5.2mm thick when open and 11.3mm when closed. It’s not a huge difference, but it makes me look forward to Apple hopefully slimming down the second-generation version, if and when it comes.

According to recent reports, the Duo is also slightly heavier than the Z Fold 8, weighing 254 grams (compared to 201 grams for Samsung’s foldable). I’m always surprised when people remark how heavy the Duo is, but I think the reason I don’t share that sentiment is that I’m accustomed to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which weighs 249 grams.

Recent findings suggest that when the Duo is open in landscape orientation, I’m glad there’s an option to split the keyboard so it’s easier to type across the wider expanse, but I wish the swipe functionality worked in that configuration, too. It’s a little thing that would make a noticeable difference for those of us who rely heavily on swipe-to-text.

One drawback of the Duo’s compact design is that some existing MagSafe wallets and other accessories won’t stick to the back without awkwardly jutting out. So you might have to invest in some newly introduced accessories specifically designed for the Duo.

Until the recent addition of face unlock, the Duo’s biggest drawback was the lack of Face ID. It’s a feature I’d expect on such a premium device, especially given that even the budget-focused iPhone 17E supports it.

Sources indicate that touch ID works reliably on the Duo, but it’s slow compared to fingerprint unlock on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (which also supports facial recognition). And while the new face unlock capability on the Duo isn’t an exact replacement for Face ID, which is more secure, it helps make accessing the phone’s contents more convenient and in line with the Duo’s modern aesthetics.

In a recent development, I’ve finished my homework: My review is done, and now, so is this one-month follow-up. What’s next?

In a recent development, I’m not sure I’m ready to throw in the towel on Apple’s foldable just yet. The novelty of the iPhone Duo hasn’t worn off, and I’ve become quite used to my passport-size companion. It does just about everything I need, despite some slight imperfections, and it’s fun to use. It’s also amusing to see how people react when they see it in my hand.

Recent findings suggest that so for now, it looks like the Duo will remain my daily driver. Whether the honeymoon phase eventually wears off remains to be seen, but I’m not in any hurry to end this love affair.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, at today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the organization introduced two fresh frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks.
  • Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model reveals 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.
  • Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, at today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the organization introduced two fresh frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model reveals 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Microsoft says MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

This doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

According to recent reports, it’s also important to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

Throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft revealed slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex.

One thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the company paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the organization’s vast product line.

Industry observers note that if you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As users adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous.

There’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

Recent findings suggest that this becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft announced MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

Sources indicate that think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the firm itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

Let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a company is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these newly introduced models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first.

Sources indicate that A company with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

Industry observers note that A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

According to recent reports, there’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

Industry observers note that microsoft says the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

Benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the latest models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open issue.

The manufacturer also described clearly that these latest models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

Speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these newly introduced models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • But does that expense result in real business value?
  • Also: Microsoft says its upcoming AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
  • It has been revealed that earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft says its upcoming AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

It has been revealed that earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

If it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s significant bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions.

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:.

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

Software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

Instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s upcoming.

What comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

According to recent reports, there’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically says, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”.

In other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving company labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the company saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your tech giant needs a chief AI officer in 2026.

Industry observers note that I find it particularly telling that this is from the firm that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

That’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

Industry observers note that microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the company’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the company’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:.

Industry observers note that this means the company doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Out. Here’s How to Make Room on Your Console

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, and it is massive.
  • In a recent development, if you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have a few options: delete games, upgrade your console’s hard drive and streaming the game.
  • The simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The wait is over. Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, and it is massive. The game is 212 GB, which means it takes up about half of the storage space on my Xbox Series S. The firm unveiled that GTA 6 is available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming without downloading it to your console. However, cloud streaming GTA 6 might affect the game’s performance and relies heavily on a strong internet connection. To avoid those challenges, I strategy on downloading the game.

In a recent development, if you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have a few options: delete games, upgrade your console’s hard drive and streaming the game. Here’s what you should know about these options.

The simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing. Uninstalling games is a good choice for folks who plan on spending a lot of time with GTA 6 and don’t intend to juggle different games. Rob Nelson, who oversees Rockstar North with Aaron Garbut, told The Latest York Times that he had an 80-hour playthrough of the game in February, so you can easily stay immersed in Grand Theft Auto’s state of Leonida.

In a recent development, you may not need to delete much – uninstalling a game like Call of Duty alone could free up nearly 315 GB, giving you enough digital storage for GTA 6. Since deleting files is almost instantaneous, you can quickly reclaim hard drive space. Because you don’t need to buy additional storage, you’ll also save a lot of money – storage prices are through the roof at the moment.

Ultimately, deleting games is a great option if you don’t want to spend any additional money or you don’t mind redownloading games later.

In a recent development, if you proposal on hopping between GTA 6 and other games, or you don’t want to delete many of your downloaded titles, you can upgrade your console’s storage. Buying storage is more expensive than deleting files from your console, but benefit from being able to seamlessly hop between Grand Theft Auto 6 and Call of Duty or Madden.

You can use internal or external storage for your console, but you might have to move files between your internal and external storage to launch games. An internal hard drive lets you seamlessly play games. Xbox consoles rely on proprietary expansion cards from Seagate or SanDisk that plug into your console for additional storage. The PlayStation 5 uses M.2 solid-state drives, which are installed alongside the PS5’s built-in storage, and CNET’s David Carnoy recommends the Lexar NM 790 as a fast SSD with a straightforward installation process.

Industry observers note that there shouldn’t be any performance, quality or load-time differences between running games from installed storage expansion devices versus your console’s internal storage. Both expansion cards and SSDs can be expensive, especially when compared with deleting games.

You could also use an external hard drive to expand your storage, which can be cheaper than buying expansion cards and internal SSD upgrades – you may even have a compatible USB external drive sitting around that you can use. However, there are caveats around what games can and can’t be played directly from external HDDs.

For Xbox consoles, some older Xbox, Xbox 360 and Xbox One titles can be stored and played from external HDDs. But games optimized for Series X/S consoles can only be stored on HDDs and must be moved back to your internal drive to play. Similarly, the PlayStation 5 only lets you store PS5 games on external HDDs, while you can store and run PS4 games from external drives.

Sources indicate that therefore, using an external HDD requires playing digital musical chairs, moving current-gen games back and forth between your external hard drive and internal console storage in order to play them. The LaCie Rugged SSD4 earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award and could be a good option. If its price tag scares you, the Western Digital P10 offers more storage at a more economical price point.

Rockstar declared that GTA 6 is available to stream on the Xbox consoles – no download required – via Xbox Cloud Gaming, with some quality and time limitations. You’ll need to buy either an Xbox Game Pass blueprint or Cloud Gaming hours. Folks who don’t want to delete games or upgrade their console storage can stream GTA 6, but you’ll need an Xbox One or Series X/S console, you won’t get the highest visual quality and you will have to pay for more playtime hours if they run out. Streaming GTA 6 could help budget-conscious gamers who don’t want to upgrade from Xbox One consoles or who don’t have the allotted storage space on their devices.

Normally, you can stream many games on PCs, mobile devices and TVs or streaming devices using Xbox Cloud Gaming or Game Pass, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is limited to the Xbox One, Series S and Series X. Additionally, GTA 6 streaming quality is capped at Series S graphical settings. So if you have a Series X, consider deleting games or upgrading your storage to run the game locally with better graphics.

While you’ll need to install the full game on your console first, remote play for Xbox and PlayStation consoles lets you stream GTA 6 to other devices, like your phone, tablet, streaming device or TV.

If you’re willing to pay a little more for the convenience of having multiple games ready to play at a moment’s notice, Xbox expansion cards or an internal SSD for a PS5 are your best options. If you want a cheaper option and don’t mind moving game files around, an external hard drive could be for you. If you have Xbox Game Pass or Xbox Cloud Gaming, you could stream the game to your console without needing more storage space. However, the cheapest option is to delete games from your internal storage and redownload them later, which can be time-consuming.

I chose the cheapest option and deleted a few games from my Xbox. I’m not planning on leaving GTA 6 any time soon.
